section_1.title: The Dimensional Paradox (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Introduce the prerequisite concept of topological dimension. Explain that a 1D line has length but no area, while a 2D square has area. Pose the question: 'Can a 1D continuous path visit every single point in a 2D area?'
section_1.example: Visualizing a thin wire (1D) trying to cover the entire surface of a silk handkerchief (2D).

section_2.title: The Peano Curve Construction (0:45-2:00)
section_2.content: Demonstrate the iterative process of space-filling curves. Start with a segment, split it into sub-segments, and refine the path recursively. Explain how infinity creates 'density'.
section_2.example: An animation showing a single line segment dividing into 9 parts, then 81, progressively folding to touch every pixel in a grid.

section_3.title: The Hilbert Curve & Locality (2:00-3:30)
section_3.content: Introduce the Hilbert curve as a practical variation. Highlight the 'Locality Principle': points close together on the curve are also close together in 2D space. This is a critical property for data mapping.
section_3.example: A digital 'Robot Gardener' traversing a square field; the Hilbert path ensures the robot minimizes travel distance while covering every inch of soil.

section_4.title: Real-World Applications (3:30-4:30)
section_4.content: Explain how space-filling curves optimize 2D data storage in 1D memory. Mention image processing (dithering) and database indexing (quadtrees).
section_4.example: A database engineer organizing massive GPS coordinates; using the Hilbert curve to store 2D map locations in a flat, high-speed 1D hard drive index.

section_5.title: Summary & Reflection (4:30-5:00)
section_5.content: Summarize the key takeaway: Space-filling curves aren't just mathematical curiosities; they are tools for mapping multi-dimensional data into linear sequences.
section_5.example: Final slide showing a beautiful, complex fractal pattern emerging from a simple iterative loop, encouraging students to think about the beauty of recursion.
